newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai zero-tariff corn quota could reach 400,000T.
newsitem.headline: Thai zero-tariff corn quota could reach 400,000T.

text.p: Thailand could double its current zero-tariff corn import quota to 400,000 tonnes, traders said on Thursday, adding that buyers are now seeking 50,000 tonnes in transit to fill the existing 200,000-tonne quota.
The Thai Feedmill Association has already petitioned the Thai government to extend the zero-tariff arrangement by a further 100,000 tonnes, association sources said on Tuesday.

"I think they're going to ask for 200,000 tonnes on top of the 200,000 tonnes they're already getting," one dealer said, adding he expected the plan to come under fire from already peeved Thai farmers.
"The politicians there will get caught in the middle of all this if they approve further imports," another trader said.
The regional grains trade is also pondering when the Philippines will come around to tendering for up to 300,000 tonnes of corn for July arrival.
The order authorising the state-run National Food Authority (NFA) to go ahead with the tender was supposed to have been issued by the office of President Fidel Ramos last week.

But the order has apparently been held up by the government's preoccupation over a row with China over a rocky outcrop in the South China Sea that Manila calls Scarborough Shoal. The arrest of 21 Chinese fishermen in the area has intensified the dispute.
"We understand the NFA is supposed to hold the tender, but it's been held up," one dealer said.
Probable sources for the corn in the tender are either U.S. or Argentine-origin, he added.
A European dealer said the corn business in the region has slowed down a bit, except for the Thai deals being done, as the trade watches the U.S. corn market.

The July corn contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) rose on Wednesday by 5-1/4 U.S. cents to end at US$2.69-1/2 a bushel. Most buyers believe prices will eventually head south on expectations of a bumper U.S. crop.

U.S. corn coming into Southeast Asia was quoted by the trade at around $138-$139 a tonne C&F for July/August shipment on a Panamax against a quote at the end of April of $149-$150 a tonne C&F for June/July shipment.
"I think the buyers here are waiting for $2.20 (a bushel) corn, but the sellers are not willing to unload this into a hole," a dealer for a European trading house said.

Malaysian feed millers are out of the market due to bumper supplies storied in their warehouses. Indonesian feedmills are likewise well-stocked although some dealers believe they will begin looking for year-end delivery later in June.
The soymeal business has also picked up slightly with dealers saying Indonesia is shopping for about 30,000-40,000 tonnes of meal for at least mid-July shipment.
Malaysia may also be interested in about 20,000 tonnes of meal for late-July shipment.
"I think there's some buying interest from Indonesia for meal," a trader said, adding though that any deal may have to wait until after parliamentary elections there this week.
Buyers in the region are largely sitting back on the belief that futures prices in Chicago will tumble further.
"Everybody here seems to think the market will fall to zero," a trader said.
